title: A theoretical study of ten N8 isomers
note_on_extraction_quality: This PDF is a scanned image with no text layer; all data below was read visually from rendered page images (pages 1-4 of the PDF). Table 2's numeric print is small; bond-length values were transcribed as legibly as possible but OCR-by-eye confidence on individual digits is MEDIUM, not high -- recommend the coordinator re-view Table 2 (page 4) and Table 1/Fig.1 (pages 2-3) directly before treating these numbers as final. No bond-ANGLE data is given anywhere in this paper (only the R_ss/R_sd/R_dd bond-length classification scheme described in the text: R_ss = bonds between two 3-coordinate atoms, R_sd = bond between a 3-coordinate and a 2-coordinate atom, R_dd/R_dd' = bonds between two 2-coordinate atoms, single or double character) -- reconstruction of full 3D geometry will need the named topology (these are the classic C8H8 hydrocarbon valence-isomer cage shapes: cubane, pentacyclooctane, cuneane, tricyclooctadienes, bicyclooctatriene, cyclooctatetraene, barrelene, pentalene) rather than these bond lengths alone.

species.notes: IMPORTANT: 'stable at HF level, but at MP2 the optimization does not converge (it was performed in C2v symmetry, i.e. in the largest abelian subgroup of D3h); the DFT calculations result in TWO IMAGINARY FREQUENCIES.' This structure is essentially NOT a confirmed minimum at any correlated level of theory (MP2 doesn't converge to a D3h stationary point at all; DFT finds 2 imaginary modes). Only the HF-level structure is a genuine stationary point. Treat with caution -- likely not a true GFN2-xTB-relaxable minimum either; may collapse to something else entirely under relaxation.
